title: Tautological clauses are satisfied by every assignment
statement: Let $c$ be a clause on the variables $x_0,\dots,x_{n-1}$, that is, a list of literals read as their disjunction, where a literal is a variable together with a sign and evaluates to that variable's value if positive and to its negation if negated. Suppose $c$ is tautological: it contains two literals on the same variable with opposite signs. Then for every Boolean assignment $x \colon \{0,\dots,n-1\} \to \{\text{true},\text{false}\}$, at least one literal of $c$ evaluates to $\mathrm{true}$, so the disjunction of the literals of $c$ evaluates to $\mathrm{true}$.
hypotheses_covered: c is a clause (list of literals)
c is tautological (two literals on the same variable with opposite signs)
x is an arbitrary Boolean assignment
replaced:
If a clause $c$ is tautological, then for every assignment $x$ the disjunction of its
literals evaluates to $\mathrm{true}$.
